confirmed_consumers.mechanism: extract_and_queue imports parse_all_tool_tags, filters tag name == intent, normalizes marker category and queues the content.
_extract_claim imports parse_all_tool_tags and accepts hypothesis marker payloads that pass claim-quality validation.

reconciliation.historical_v27_claim: intent and hypothesis were not dead registry tools; they were marker protocols consumed by separate runtime subsystems.
reconciliation.promotion: The marker-vs-executable-tool distinction is no longer merely historical inference; both named marker consumers are present in the current Project-Frankenstein source snapshot.
reconciliation.limit: This confirms code presence and parsing paths, not that every deployment instance currently runs/enables those services. Runtime-process liveness remains a separate operational check.

needle: Do not place intent/hypothesis event markers in the executable capability registry merely because they share legacy <tool> syntax.
Migrate legacy shared syntax toward explicit event/marker IR while preserving consumer compatibility during transition.
claycode: Introduce distinct IR node kinds for EffectCall and CognitiveMarker/Event; compile legacy <tool> wrappers only at compatibility boundaries.
harness: Gate marker exceptions on source-level consumer existence and separately test deployment/runtime liveness when operational truth matters.
Add a regression that removing a marker consumer makes the compatibility guard fail rather than silently whitelisting the marker forever.
claygraph: Create explicit consumer edges intent->intent_queue and hypothesis->hypothesis_engine; liveness-backed compatibility depends on those edges.
unifieddb: Store marker schemas separately from tool capability schemas and version their consumers independently.
gwt: Intent/hypothesis events are cognitive-state candidates, not executable effects; workspace routing should preserve that distinction.
